newsitem.title: USA: Classic Sports files FCC suit vs Cablevision.
newsitem.headline: Classic Sports files FCC suit vs Cablevision.

text.p: Classic Sports Network, an independent cable TV operator, said Monday it filed a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission accusing Cablevision Systems Corp of violating the 1992 Cable Act.
Classic Sports also said it would vigorously oppose Cablevision's agreement to buy the 50 percent stake held by ITT Corp in the Madison Square Garden, a mecca for sports and entertainment events.

In its complaint, it alleged that Cablevision violated the federal law by demanding an ownership interest in Classic Sports and exclusive distribution rights to its programming as a "precondition" to carrying the network on Cablevision's cable TV systems. Classic said it is now carried in fewer than 50,000 of Cablevision's 2.8 million cable homes nationwide.

Brian Bedol, chief executive officer of Classic Sports, alleged Cablevision has "engaged in a consistent and conscious pattern of coercive conduct over a two-year period in an attempt to control not just access to programming, but the programming itself."
Cablevision and ITT teamed up in 1995 to buy Madison Square Garden, which also has a cable television network, for $1.0 billion and each holds a 50 percent interest.
Classic Sports said Cablevision's apparent strategy was to dominate sports television programming and distribution in New York, "to the exclusion of competitive or independent programmers.
"The end-result of such a strategy, especially in light of Cablevision's history of anti-competitive behavior, would likely constitute a violation of federal antitrust laws," Bedol said.

Classic Sports said it filed its complaint under Section 616 of the 1992 law which aims to prevent cable systems and other multichannel video programming distributors from taking undue advantage of programming vendors through various practices, including coercing vendors to grant ownership interests or exclusive distribution rights in exchange for carriage on their systems.
Earlier this month, when Classic Sports said it intended to file the FCC complaint, Cablevision issued a statement denying it had broken the 1992 law.
